title: 15 Finalists Named in Global Quantum + AI Challenge
html:
Insider Brief

  • Fifteen teams have reached the finals of the Global Quantum + AI Challenge to develop working proofs of concept addressing five industry problems.
  • Selected from 380 applications across 86 countries, the finalists will compete for $200,000 in prizes across challenges from Airbus, Cleveland Clinic, E.ON, HSBC and Volkswagen Group.
  • The second phase runs from Nov. 16 to Feb. 28, 2027, with finalists receiving access to Classiq’s quantum design platform and AWS cloud computing resources.

Fifteen teams have been named finalists in the Global Quantum + AI Challenge, advancing to develop working proofs of concept for industry problems ranging from drug discovery to credit card fraud detection.

The competition offers $200,000 in prizes across five challenges, with $40,000 allocated to each. Its enterprise partners are Airbus, Cleveland Clinic, E.ON, HSBC and Volkswagen Group.

The finalists were selected from 380 challenge applications from 86 countries submitted before the first phase closed Sept. 15, 2026, according to the organizers. Each enterprise partner, working with ecosystem partner MITRE, selected three finalists for its challenge.

The second phase begins Nov. 16, when finalists will start turning their proposals into working proofs of concept. Teams will have access to Classiq’s quantum design platform and cloud computing resources from Amazon Web Services. Submissions are due Feb. 28, 2027.

A jury of academic and enterprise experts will then select the winners. Jurors announced so far include Elham Kashefi of the National Quantum Computing Centre and the University of Edinburgh; Travis Humble of the Quantum Science Center at Oak Ridge National Laboratory; and Marc Fischer of Airbus.

“What we’ve seen in Phase 1 is proof that quantum talent exists everywhere. Builders from over 50 countries showed up to tackle problems from Airbus, HSBC, E.ON, Cleveland Clinic, and Volkswagen Group,” said Alex Challans, CEO, Resonance. “That’s the kind of global collaboration this industry needs more of.”

The finalists

Airbus: Quantum solvers for enhancing predictive aerodynamic modeling

The challenge seeks quantum computing approaches to improve predictions of how air flows around aircraft and other products.

  • planqc Quantum Solutions: planqc GmbH, Germany.
  • Georgia Tech / Qscico: Georgia Institute of Technology, United States.
  • AeroTN: Aegiq, with Oak Ridge National Laboratory, NVIDIA and the University of Massachusetts Amherst, United Kingdom.

Cleveland Clinic: Unlocking undruggable targets with quantum simulation of allosteric signal propagation

The challenge focuses on simulating how signals travel through proteins, potentially helping researchers identify sites where drugs could act on targets that are difficult to treat with existing approaches.

  • Percene: Percene Systems, Australia.
  • QBIT Lab (QWallo): University of Cambridge / Yonsei University, United Kingdom.
  • AlloWalk: A multi-institution consortium including National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University and the University of Cambridge, Taiwan.

E.ON: Quantum-enabled grid expansion planning for distribution energy networks

The challenge examines how quantum computing could help utilities decide where and how to expand electricity distribution networks.

  • JIJ Team: Jij Inc. / University of Bristol, Japan.
  • 4colors Research: United Kingdom.
  • team17: Yale University / Old Dominion University / Travelers, United States.

HSBC: Quantum-enhanced credit card fraud detection for digital payment ecosystems

The challenge explores whether quantum computing can improve the detection of fraudulent card transactions.

  • CSIRO / Monash: CSIRO with Monash University, Australia.
  • Rashtriya Raksha University: India.
  • HCM_Uni: An academic team based in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.

Volkswagen Group: Quantum-enhanced Vision-Language-Action models for autonomous driving and robotics

The challenge seeks to improve models that combine visual information and language instructions to guide actions in autonomous vehicles and robots.

  • Quantum Pulse: Qkrishi, India.
  • Mimos: MIMOS Berhad, Malaysia.
  • Artificial Brain: United States.

Program support

MITRE serves as the competition’s ecosystem partner, AWS provides cloud computing resources, and Classiq provides its quantum design platform. South Carolina Quantum leads the program’s Local Deployment Stream.

Further information about the five industry challenges is available on the Global Quantum + AI Challenge website.

MENTIONED IN THE ARTICLE

Airbus, founded in 1970, is a global European aerospace corporation and one of the world's largest manufacturer of airliners. Headquartered in Leiden, Netherlands, with major operations in France, Germany, Spain, and the UK, the company specializes in designing, manufacturing, and supporting commercial aircraft, helicopters, defense systems, and space technology.

Cleveland Clinic functions as a not-for-profit academic medical institution, seamlessly merging clinical and hospital care with research and educational endeavors. The institution is dedicated to enhancing medical treatment for the unwell, delving into the intricacies of their ailments, and advancing the knowledge of those in the medical profession. In a significant milestone, Cleveland Clinic achieved the distinction of being the inaugural healthcare provider in the United States to join the United Nations Global Compact as a signatory in 2008, following the second worldwide.

The E.ON Group is one of Europe's largest operators of energy networks and energy infrastructure and a provider of innovative customer solutions for 50 million customers.

HSBC stands as a global bank, possessing assets amounting to USD 3 trillion and serving a customer base of 40 million individuals across the world. Its operational footprint extends across 64 countries, supported by approximately 220,000 full-time employees. The bank maintains significant presence in regions such as Asia, Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, and North America. Notably, the United Kingdom and Hong Kong stand as the bank's largest markets. HSBC's services encompass a wide range, including retail, commercial, and institutional banking, global banking and markets, as well as wealth management and private banking.

Volkswagen is a German multinational automotive manufacturing corporation headquartered in Wolfsburg, Lower Saxony, Germany

Classiq Technologies specializes in quantum computing software, focusing on enabling the design, optimization, analysis, and deployment of quantum algorithms. It develops a high-level quantum algorithm design platform (IDE, compiler, “OS”) that transforms functional models into optimized, hardware-aware quantum circuits to address the challenge of gate-level complexity. It emphasizes abstraction, circuit synthesis, and resource optimization, working with enterprises, researchers, and hardware/cloud providers to deliver scalable quantum software.
